ig_carousel_topic.topic: The Kelly criterion — explained without the math degree
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you actually bet?
Most bettors guess. Kelly gives you a framework.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake: flat-betting every play the same amount regardless of edge.
But not every edge is equal — so why treat them that way?
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Kelly says: bet a fraction of your bankroll proportional to your edge.
Bigger edge = bigger bet. Smaller edge = smaller bet. No edge = no bet.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: You have a 55% win probability on a -110 line (break-even is 52.4%).
Full Kelly suggests ~4.5% of bankroll. Most sharps use Half Kelly (2.25%) to reduce variance.
On a $1,000 roll: that's a $22.50 play — not $100.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
You don't need the formula memorized.
You need the idea: size your bets to match your confidence, not your emotions.
Save this and revisit it every time you're tempted to chase.
